stories.headline: ULA's Vulcan fails 10 minutes into flight, destroying 40 Amazon Leo satellites

key_facts.fact: A United Launch Alliance Vulcan rocket lifted off from Cape Canaveral at 12:40 p.m. EST on Sunday, Nov. 15, carrying 40 Amazon Leo satellites, and suffered an anomaly about 10 minutes into flight, failing to reach orbit.
key_facts.excerpt: "we confirm that the Vulcan vehicle launched from Space Launch Complex 41 ... suffered an anomaly 10 minutes into the flight and failed to deliver the Amazon mission to orbit," ULA said ... The 214-foot-tall Vulcan blasted off from pad 41 ... at 12:40 p.m. EST

key_facts.fact: It was ULA's first outright mission failure since the Boeing-Lockheed Martin joint venture was formed in 2006.
key_facts.excerpt: It was the first outright failure of a United Launch Alliance rocket since the company, a partnership between Boeing and Lockheed Martin, was formed in 2006.

key_facts.fact: The failure occurred during the burn of the Centaur upper stage; the cause has not been identified.
key_facts.excerpt: The anomaly came about 10 minutes into the flight, during the Centaur's burn, according to Spaceflight Now ... ULA hasn't identified the cause.

key_facts.fact: This was Vulcan's fifth flight and its first in nine months, after a stand-down to fix solid rocket booster nozzle problems; the 40 satellites, weighing over 50,000 lb, were ULA's heaviest payload ever.
key_facts.excerpt: On its fifth mission ... With the 40 Amazon satellites weighing more than 50,000 lb., Vulcan Leo 1 represented not only the heaviest payload for ULA's new booster, but the company's heaviest payload ever

key_facts.fact: The launch was the first of 38 Vulcan flights Amazon bought for Leo, its Starlink rival; Vulcan is slated to carry more than 1,500 first-generation Leo satellites.
key_facts.excerpt: The flight was Vulcan's first in nine months, and the first of 38 Vulcan launches that Amazon has purchased ... is slated to carry more than 1,500 of Amazon's first-generation satellites

key_facts.fact: Before the failure Amazon had launched 396 Leo satellites on 14 missions since April 2025; the constellation needs more than 3,200.
key_facts.excerpt: Before Sunday, Amazon had launched 396 satellites for its Redmond-based satellite internet network, formerly known as Project Kuiper, on 14 missions since April 2025.

key_facts.fact: Amazon said there is risk with any launch, especially inaugural missions, and that it still trusts ULA as a partner.
key_facts.excerpt: Amazon projected confidence in its launch partner despite the failure, posting on X that, "There is risk with any launch, and that's especially true for inaugural missions like LV-01."

stories.headline: China confirms first Trump-Xi-Putin summit for Nov. 19 in Shenzhen as Trump leaves for Asia

key_facts.fact: China's Foreign Ministry confirmed on Monday, Nov. 16, that Xi Jinping will hold a China-Russia-US heads-of-state meeting with Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump in Shenzhen on Thursday, Nov. 19, the first such three-way meeting.
key_facts.excerpt: "On November 19, Chinese President Xi Jinping will hold a China-Russia-U.S. heads of state meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin and U.S. President Donald Trump in Shenzhen," the Foreign Ministry said

key_facts.fact: The White House confirmed the meeting on Friday, Nov. 13, and the Kremlin on Saturday; a White House spokeswoman said Trump will discuss reducing nuclear weapons.
key_facts.excerpt: Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov confirmed Saturday ... The White House also confirmed the meeting on Friday. "Among other topics, he will discuss the reduction of nuclear weapons in the world"

key_facts.fact: US officials said Trump will raise the Iran war but does not intend to discuss Ukraine in the trilateral, and do not expect a concrete agreement on denuclearization.
key_facts.excerpt: The president is expected to discuss the war in Iran with Xi and Russian President Vladimir Putin. However, he does not intend to discuss Ukraine ... officials said they do not anticipate the leaders reaching any concrete agreement

key_facts.fact: Trump leaves Washington on Monday, Nov. 16, for Manila (Quad meeting, a trade deal with Thailand) before Shenzhen, where he will hold a bilateral meeting and working lunch with Xi on Thursday; no Trump-Putin bilateral is planned.
key_facts.excerpt: Trump is expected to leave Washington in the morning of Monday, Nov. 16 and arrive in Manila ... The president is also expected to sign a trade deal with Thailand ... Trump and Putin will not be meeting one-on-one separately

key_facts.fact: The 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting runs Nov. 18-19 in Shenzhen, chaired by Xi; the APEC CEO Summit is Nov. 17-18.
key_facts.excerpt: The 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting will be held in Shenzhen from November 18 to 19 ... The APEC CEO Summit will be held in Shenzhen from November 17 to 18

key_facts.fact: Analysts expect few deliverables from the Trump-Xi meeting; the US-China trade truce runs until January 2027 and the two leaders are due to meet again at the G20 in Florida in December.
key_facts.excerpt: Neither side is preparing ambitious deliverables for this meeting ... the two countries' trade truce would be extended by two months until January 2027

stories.headline: Zelensky says US floated NATO membership for Ukraine if it leaves Donbas; Kremlin rebuffs

key_facts.fact: Zelensky said US negotiators asked, for the first time in the peace talks, whether Ukraine would withdraw from the Donbas in exchange for joining NATO.
key_facts.excerpt: "The Americans raised a question: 'What if Ukraine joins NATO? Would Ukraine withdraw from Donbas?" he said. ... This is the first time the question of linking NATO membership to territorial concessions has been raised

key_facts.fact: Zelensky reiterated Kyiv would not give up territory, but said that with a deal including security guarantees, a strong army and reconstruction funds, he would put the territorial question to a national referendum.
key_facts.excerpt: if Ukraine received a peace deal which included security guarantees, the right to maintain a strong and well-funded Ukrainian army, and funds to rebuild the country, then he would hold a national referendum on the question of ceding territory

key_facts.fact: On Nov. 14, US envoy Jared Kushner said on X that Washington will now focus on facilitating direct engagement between Moscow and European partners and preparing the next trilateral round, which has no date.
key_facts.excerpt: Washington would now focus on "facilitating direct engagement between Moscow and European partners" and on preparing the agenda for the next round of three-way talks ... No date or venue for that round has been announced.

key_facts.fact: Kushner wrote that both sides privately understand practical compromises will be needed and that several new ideas are being explored.
key_facts.excerpt: "In our private discussions, both sides understand that practical compromises will be necessary to end this war."

key_facts.fact: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said a Ukraine settlement is inseparable from a new European security architecture and that, if Europe does not want peace, Russia will have to achieve its goals by force.
key_facts.excerpt: "Se in realtà non vogliono la pace, sarà tutto inutile. In tal caso, vista l'assenza di margini per un negoziato, dovremo procedere con la forza"

key_facts.fact: Russia renewed its demand for NATO to pull troops back from the alliance's eastern flank, a likely nonstarter for Europe ahead of the next round, in which European partners are expected to take part.
key_facts.excerpt: Russia reportedly renewed its demands for NATO to withdraw troops from the bloc's eastern flank ... European partners are expected to join the next round of talks, with Moscow's demand for a NATO pullback likely a nonstarter for Europe.

stories.headline: Estonia to close all Russia border crossings from Dec. 1 after GRU-ordered attack on drone maker

key_facts.fact: In the early hours of Nov. 14, intruders tried to break into drone maker Threod Systems in Viimsi, near Tallinn, aiming to cause an explosion and set the building on fire; company security stopped them.
key_facts.excerpt: the suspects attempted to cause an explosion and set fire to the company's premises in Viimsi, near Tallinn, at around 3:00 a.m local time ... No injuries or significant damage were reported.

key_facts.fact: Eight suspects, all residents of Latvia, were detained; Estonia's Internal Security Service (KAPO) said the attack was ordered by Russia's GRU military intelligence.
key_facts.excerpt: Eight suspects, all residents of neighboring Latvia, were detained ... KAPO, said intelligence gathered by its officers showed the attack was commissioned by Russia's GRU military intelligence agency.

key_facts.fact: Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna announced on Nov. 15 that Estonia will close its road border crossings with Russia from Dec. 1, saying it would curb hostile activity and sanctions circumvention.
key_facts.excerpt: The Government of Estonia plans to close its road border crossings with Russia from 1 December in response to a sabotage attempt targeting the Estonian defence industry company Threod Systems, commissioned by Russia's military intelligence agency GRU.

key_facts.fact: Estonia has three road crossings with Russia, at Narva, Luhamaa and Koidula; it is the second attempted arson on an Estonian defense firm since August, after Milrem Robotics.
key_facts.excerpt: Estonia has three open road border crossings with Russia in Narva, Luhamaa and Koidula ... This is the second attempted arson attack on a defense industry company since August, when Milrem Robotics, which is based in Tallinn, was targeted.

key_facts.fact: The Kremlin called the accusations entirely baseless; Peskov likened the closure to Estonia building a wall.
key_facts.excerpt: "They are entirely baseless. We therefore cannot accept such accusations" ... "it's as if Estonia is building a wall," he added.

key_facts.fact: Tsahkna said he would push for tougher sanctions and stricter visa policy at the Nov. 16 meeting of EU foreign ministers in Brussels.
key_facts.excerpt: he will discuss increasing pressure on Russia at Monday's meeting of EU foreign ministers in Brussels ... This means tougher sanctions, a stricter visa policy

stories.headline: Iran fires drones at US base in Bahrain twice in three days; oil slides as IEA sees glut

key_facts.fact: On Friday, Nov. 13, US Central Command said it shot down two Iranian drones headed toward Bahrain; on Sunday the IRGC said it launched six drones at a US air defense radar at Riffa Air Base, which Bahrain's military said it destroyed.
key_facts.excerpt: On Friday, US Central Command said it shot down two Iranian drones headed toward Bahrain ... Two days later, the IRGC said it launched six drones at a US air defense radar at Riffa Air Base. Bahrain's military said it destroyed the attacks

key_facts.fact: The strikes were Iran's first on Bahrain in about two months.
key_facts.excerpt: They were the first strikes on Bahrain in about two months. Yet oil prices extended a two-week slump.

key_facts.fact: The International Energy Agency said on Friday that global oil supply exceeds demand for the first time since the war began, with a surplus of about 2 million barrels a day expected this quarter, and that members would speed up emergency stock releases.
key_facts.excerpt: On Friday, the International Energy Agency (IEA) said global supply exceeded demand for the first time since the war began. The IEA expects a surplus of about 2 million barrels a day this quarter ... members would speed up the release of emergency stockpiles.

key_facts.fact: Brent fell 0.49% to $95.37 a barrel early Monday, Nov. 16, and WTI to $88.33, as Middle East shipments through Hormuz were nearly restored to pre-war levels.
key_facts.excerpt: Brent futures were down 47 cents, or 0.49%, to $95.37 a barrel by 0145 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude fell 23 cents, or 0.26%, to $88.33.

key_facts.fact: Iranian parliament speaker Ghalibaf said the war could end if Washington accepted Tehran's 'logical conditions', while a US official said a third US carrier strike group, the USS Theodore Roosevelt, arrived in the Central Command area on Sunday.
key_facts.excerpt: Ghalibaf saying the war could end if Washington accepted Tehran's "logical conditions" ... The USS Theodore Roosevelt aircraft carrier arrived in the Central Command area of responsibility on Sunday ... Washington now has three aircraft carrier strike groups

stories.headline: US producer prices rise 6.5% a year, most since 2022, locking in a December Fed hike

key_facts.fact: The US producer price index rose 0.3% in October, below the 0.4% forecast, but 6.5% from a year earlier, the highest annual rate since November 2022, the BLS reported on Friday, Nov. 13.
key_facts.excerpt: The producer price index ... rose a seasonally adjusted 0.3% for the month, against the Dow Jones consensus for a 0.4% increase ... headline PPI accelerated 6.5%, up 0.2 percentage point for the highest annual rate since November 2022.

key_facts.fact: Truck freight transport accounted for more than 80% of the rise in services costs, a sign of diesel prices spreading through the economy.
key_facts.excerpt: Truck transport of freight last month generated more than 80% of the increase in the cost of services, the BLS said.

key_facts.fact: Markets fully price at least a quarter-point hike at the Fed's Dec. 8-9 meeting, with slight odds of a half-point move; the Fed's rate sits at 3.75%-4%.
key_facts.excerpt: Markets are fully pricing in a quarter percentage point increase in the central bank's key overnight borrowing rate, with slight odds that the Federal Open Market Committee might opt for a half-point hike.

key_facts.fact: San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly said on Friday the Fed will 'in all likelihood' need to raise rates; Boston Fed President Susan Collins said some additional tightening soon is appropriate.
key_facts.excerpt: "We're going to need to, in all likelihood, raise rates," Daly predicted.

key_facts.fact: The 10-year Treasury yield closed Friday at 5.15% and the dollar index rose to a 1.5-year high.
key_facts.excerpt: The 10-year Treasury yield closed at 5.15% and the 2-year at 4.88% ... The dollar index rose to a 1.5-year high

key_facts.fact: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh moderates a panel in San Francisco on Monday, Nov. 16, on findings of a Fed task force on productivity and jobs, including AI's effects; October FOMC minutes follow on Wednesday.
key_facts.excerpt: On Monday, Chairman Kevin Warsh will moderate a panel in San Francisco, with the event likely to revolve around the findings of a Fed panel established by Warsh to investigate productivity and jobs.

stories.headline: FDA approves Roche's Gazyva as first drug for primary membranous nephropathy

key_facts.fact: The FDA approved Gazyva (obinutuzumab) on Nov. 13 to induce remission of proteinuria in adults with primary membranous nephropathy at risk of progression, the first drug approved specifically for the kidney disease.
key_facts.excerpt: The FDA approved Gazyva on Nov. 13, per the agency's announcement ... The FDA says Gazyva is the first drug approved specifically for this disease.

key_facts.fact: In the phase 3 MAJESTY trial of 142 adults, 36% of Gazyva patients reached complete remission at week 104 versus 6% on tacrolimus, per the FDA.
key_facts.excerpt: The FDA reported complete remission at week 104 in 36% of Gazyva patients and 6% of tacrolimus patients.

key_facts.fact: Grade 3 or higher adverse events occurred in 22% of obinutuzumab patients versus 19% on tacrolimus; the label carries boxed warnings for hepatitis B reactivation and PML.
key_facts.excerpt: Safety was broadly comparable to tacrolimus, with grade ≥3 AEs 22% vs 19% and serious AEs 17% vs 14%, alongside boxed warnings for HBV reactivation and PML.

key_facts.fact: The approval carried Breakthrough Therapy, Orphan Drug and Priority Review designations; no therapy had previously been approved by the FDA or EMA for the disease.
key_facts.excerpt: Regulatory momentum included Breakthrough Therapy, Orphan Drug, and Priority Review designations, addressing a PMN landscape previously lacking FDA/EMA-approved therapies

key_facts.fact: On the same day the FDA also approved AstraZeneca's Imfinzi plus Padcev before and after bladder removal for cisplatin-ineligible muscle-invasive bladder cancer, after the VOLGA trial showed a 42% lower risk of death versus surgery-based care.
key_facts.excerpt: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration on Friday, Nov. 13, approved AstraZeneca's Imfinzi with Padcev ... In the VOLGA trial, the pairing lowered the risk of death 42% compared with surgery-based care
